title: Betanin protects against diabetic retinal damage via the inhibition of NF-kappaB/NLRP3/VEGF axis: Insights from network pharmacology and experimental studies.
authors: Zaitone, Sawsan; Soliman, Nema; Shalaby, Amany M; Abdelgbar, Ahmed A; Saleh, Mohamed A K; Farrag, Ahmed A; Elaskary, Abdelhakeem A; Abu El Wafa, Esam Ghanem; Eltrawy, Amira H; Hisham, Fatma Azzahraa; Abdelkhalig, Sozan M; El-Sayed, Rehab M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究甜菜苷通过抑制NF-kappaB/NLRP3/VEGF轴保护糖尿病视网膜病变，虽含分子对接但核心为湿实验验证，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DIR) is a predominant diabetic microvascular complication that may cause vision loss. Retinal inflammation and angiogenesis contribute largely to the neuronal degeneration in DIR. The current study is aiming to test the effect of oral betanin doses in protection from DIR in rats along with a network pharmacology study to investigate an assumption that betanin may inhibit nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kappaB). Three rat groups were assigned as vehicle, DIR, and DIR + Betanin 100 mg/kg. Molecular docking indicated the possible binding between betanin and NF-kappaB while the bioinformatic study highlighted a relation between this possible inhibition and suppression of NOD-like receptor pyrin domain-containing protein 3/vascular endothelial growth factor (NLRP3/VEGF) axis. The rat experimental study validated this assumption and indicated a protective effect for betanin on rat retinas as shown by routine hematoxylin and eosin staining (retinal thickness and ganglion cell count) and periodic acid-Schiff staining that was mediated through mitigating expression/protein level for of NF-kappaB, NLRP3, TNF-alpha, IL-6 and VEGF proteins. Immunohistochemistry showed that betanin was able to suppress retinal content of the glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). In conclusion, the current study indicated that betanin was a good candidate for DIR in rats through suppression of the inflammatory cascade and may be suggested for diabetic patients if appropriated clinical studies will be available.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病视网膜病变（diabetic retinopathy, DIR）是一种主要的糖尿病微血管并发症，可能导致视力丧失。视网膜炎症和血管生成在很大程度上促进了DIR中的神经元变性。本研究旨在测试口服甜菜红素（betanin）剂量对大鼠DIR的保护作用，并采用网络药理学研究来探讨甜菜红素可能抑制核因子-κB（nuclear factor-kappa B, NF-kappaB）的假设。将三组大鼠分别设为载体组、DIR组和DIR+甜菜红素100 mg/kg组。分子对接表明甜菜红素与NF-kappaB之间可能存在结合，而生物信息学研究则强调了这种可能抑制与NOD样受体热蛋白结构域相关蛋白3/血管内皮生长因子（NLRP3/VEGF）轴抑制之间的关系。大鼠实验研究验证了这一假设，并通过常规苏木精-伊红染色（视网膜厚度和神经节细胞计数）及高碘酸-希夫染色显示，甜菜红素对大鼠视网膜具有保护作用，这种作用是通过减轻NF-kappaB、NLRP3、TNF-alpha、IL-6和VEGF蛋白的表达/蛋白水平介导的。免疫组织化学显示，甜菜红素能够抑制视网膜中胶质纤维酸性蛋白（glial fibrillary acidic protein, GFAP）的含量。总之，本研究表明，甜菜红素通过抑制炎症级联反应，是大鼠DIR的良好候选药物，若未来有适当的临床研究，可能建议用于糖尿病患者。
